title: Cross-SDK streaming iterator + pagination helpers for embeddings & rerank
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Provide a memory-efficient, language-idiomatic iterator/streaming abstraction across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs for the Embeddings and Rerank endpoints. Goal is API parity for common patterns: pagination, batching, retries with backoff, and streaming ergonomics (async generators in Python/TS, channel-based iterators in Go). This reduces duplication in customer code and makes common large-input workflows easy and reliable (e.g., chunked document embedding, batched reranking of search candidates).
background: Customers frequently reimplement pagination + batching + retry logic around /embeddings and /rerank. Existing SDK helpers are inconsistent across languages (some provide batch helpers, others require manual loops). This causes bugs, memory spikes, and nonstandard retry behaviors that complicate production usage. We need an opinionated, well-documented iterator surface that is memory-efficient, supports streaming results, and respects platform backpressure and retry semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Python: provide an async generator `stream_embeddings` and sync iterator `iter_embeddings` that yield per-item embeddings and optionally batched lists; supports `batch_size`, `max_concurrency`, `retry_policy`, and `max_memory_mb` parameters.
TypeScript: provide async iterable `client.streamEmbeddings()` with the same option names and behavior parity with Python (including abort signal handling for cancellation).
Go: provide `EmbeddingIterator` (channel-based) and helper `StreamEmbeddings` that returns a lightweight iterator with context cancellation and backpressure semantics.
Rerank: equivalents for rerank endpoints that accept candidate streams and yield ranked results incrementally.
Common retry policy implemented in SDK core, with deterministic retryable error set and exponential backoff; retried requests are observable in logs/metrics.

Examples: 3 cross-language example notebooks/snippets for (1) streaming large corpus embeddings with fixed memory, (2) batched rerank of search candidates with early stopping, (3) combined embed->rerank pipeline with pipelined concurrency.
Docs: console docs and README snippets added; design doc and API surface approved by SDK leads.
implementation_notes: Design an SDK-core primitive `PagedStream` that composes pagination (server cursors) and local batching; language-specific wrappers convert to idiomatic iterators/async iterables.
Expose `max_memory_mb` to limit in-flight batches; use streaming decoder for large responses to avoid buffering entire payloads.
Retry semantics: use central `RetryPolicy` with idempotency rules; embedding and rerank are read-only so can be retried safely for transient failures; provide opt-out for exact-once semantics.
Backpressure: TS/py use async/await + semaphore for concurrency; Go uses buffered channels and honors context cancellation.
Telemetry: emit events for `stream.start`, `stream.batch_sent`, `stream.retry`, `stream.error` with tags (model, endpoint, batch_size) to enable cost and latency analysis in Console.
Performance: re-use HTTP connections, prefer chunked responses, and provide an option to turn on server-side batching hints when available.
Edge cases: handle partial batch failures (retry subset), dedupe candidate IDs for rerank, and provide an option to short-circuit on confidence threshold.
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: RFC drafted and shared with SDK leads. Proposed core primitive `PagedStream` and language adapters.

2026-03-03: Architecture sync with Python, TS, Go leads. Agreed on async generator parity and central retry policy. Decided to surface `max_memory_mb` and `max_inflight_batches` as primary safety knobs.
2026-03-07: Python prototype implemented (`iter_embeddings` + `stream_embeddings`) using aiohttp stream decoding; unit tests for memory cap added.
2026-03-09: TS prototype implemented as async iterable; added AbortSignal support and example in `examples/stream-embeddings.ts`.
2026-03-11: Go iterator design approved in doc; started implementation of `embedding.Iterator` with context cancellation and channel semantics.
2026-03-12: Initial cross-language example draft complete. Preparing PRs and QA plan.
qa_plan: Unit tests for iterator yield shapes, memory cap, retry behavior (simulate transient 5xx and connection resets).
Integration tests against staging runtime using large payloads to verify chunked decoding and memory usage under 150MB.
Load test: pipeline embed->rerank with 10k docs and concurrent consumer to validate throughput and backpressure.
Cross-language behavioral tests: run Python/TS/Go example scripts in CI and assert identical outputs for deterministic seeds.
Manual review: SDK leads to validate ergonomics and docs before release.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Language parity drift if implementation details leak into public surface. Mitigation: keep `PagedStream` internal and only document stable iterator APIs; require SDK lead sign-off for changes.
Risk: Memory leaks in streaming decoding. Mitigation: enforce `max_memory_mb` and CI memory regression tests.
Risk: Unexpected partial failures when retrying batched requests. Mitigation: implement idempotent chunk boundaries and per-item retry when supported by runtime (and surface opt-out flag).
reviews_and_feedback: 2026-03-04 (Emily Park, SDK-Python): Prefer explicit async generator names (`stream_embeddings`) rather than overloading `embeddings()` to return either list or generator.
2026-03-05 (Jasper Liu, SDK-TS): Suggest exposing AbortSignal early to allow graceful cancellation in browser contexts.
2026-03-08 (Rohit Menon, Infra): Add telemetry hooks for stream retry events so we can correlate cost spikes to retries.
2026-03-10 (Design): Example snippets need a small diagram showing pipelined concurrency for embed->rerank to help adoption.
next_steps: Open PRs for Python (draft), TS (draft), and Go (WIP) and link CI jobs: ensure cross-language tests are green.
Add example notebooks to /examples and publish docs pages with snippets and migration notes.
Coordinate with Console team to add `stream.*` telemetry to SDK ingestion pipeline.
Plan post-release experiment to measure reduction in customer-side code duplication and error rates (instrument adoption via feature flag).
